chapters.title: Product search indexes
chapters.subtitle: Search that ranks the best match first

steps.text: A listing searches your database by default. This video shows how to turn on a product search feature, create the index, choose it on a listing, and what visitors see.

chapters.title: Why a search index
chapters.subtitle: Search that ranks the best match first

steps.text: By default, a listing searches your database. For most catalogs, that is exactly right.
A large catalog, or one where the best match should come first, can search a search server instead.
The visitors see the same filters, counts, sorts and pages. Keyword search matches the start of words, such as fo for Ford, and ranks the best matches first.
Turning on a search feature is not enough. You also create the index, and choose it on the listing.
First, turn on a product search feature: Elasticsearch, Lucene or Azure AI Search. Lucene keeps its index on your own server and needs nothing else.
Second, under Search, Indexes, add a products index, and save. It fills with your products in the background.
Third, edit a listing, pick the index under Search index, and publish.
Elasticsearch and Azure AI Search need their connection set up first.
Open Tools, Features, and search for Product Search. Click Enable next to Product Search, Lucene. Lucene itself is turned on with it.
Open Search, Indexes. Next to Products, Lucene, click Add.
Enter a name for the index, and click Save. The index fills with your products in the background, and the list shows its status.
Open Commerce, Product Listings, and edit the listing. Under Search index, which is shown once an index exists, choose the index you created, instead of the database. Click Publish.
On the shop, visitors search as before. Type the start of a word, and the listing shows the products that match, with the same filters and counts.
Each change to a product reaches the index when it is published, and the index rebuilds itself when you change your product types or their fields.
If the search server cannot be reached, the listing searches the database instead, so it keeps working.
Elasticsearch and Azure AI Search work the same way, with Products, Elasticsearch and Products, Azure AI Search indexes.
The listing's keyword search can be turned off, and a listing with no filters and no search has no filters panel.
A search index is not needed for a small shop. Add one when the database search is slow, or the ranking matters.
